commitments.check_or_counterexample: Contradicted if exposed and naive communities show no differences in strain-level genotypes, gene or protein expression, heat-shock phenotypes, or interaction assays immediately before the new pulse, or if reconstituting both from the same measured species abundances reproduces the faster recovery.
commitments.claim: Faster recovery in the previously exposed community is caused by a prior-exposure legacy not captured by equal measured species abundances, such as within-species physiological/strain-level differences or altered community interactions.

commitments.check_or_counterexample: Contradicted or inadequate if this investigation cannot distinguish transient acclimation from heritable strain sorting, or if the recovery advantage disappears when communities are reconstituted from the same measured species abundances.
commitments.claim: The most helpful next investigation is to combine strain-resolved metagenomics/metatranscriptomics with isolate-level heat-tolerance assays and a reciprocal transplant/common-garden or memory-decay time course before and after the new pulse.

accepted_steps.derivation: The only equal measured state is species abundances immediately before the new heat pulse. Therefore the faster recovery of the previously exposed community cannot be attributed to the measured abundance profile. The remaining explanations are sub-abundance biological differences: within-species physiological acclimation or stress memory, selection or sorting of heat-tolerant strains/genotypes, or altered community interactions or extracellular environment. These alternatives are not distinguished by the available evidence. The most discriminating next investigation should measure within-species and functional state before and after the pulse while also testing whether any recovery advantage persists, transfers, or decays without further heat selection. A combined strain-resolved metagenomic/metatranscriptomic survey, isolate-level heat-tolerance assays, and a reciprocal transplant/common-garden or memory-decay arm would separate transient plasticity from heritable selection and environmental carryover.
accepted_steps.goal: Explain the faster recovery by identifying a prior-exposure legacy not visible in measured abundances, and choose the most discriminating next investigation.
accepted_steps.result:
The difference is most plausibly produced by a cryptic prior-exposure legacy—within-species acclimation, strain-level sorting, or modified community interactions—not by the equal measured species abundances. The most helpful next investigation is a strain-resolved functional profiling and common-garden/transplant experiment with a memory-decay arm.
